data.narrative:
Critical Loop, a Series A climate and energy company founded by Bala Ramamurthy, has raised $49M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of nine firms in the Climate & Energy sector—one public entity and eight private companies including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Given the nascent stage and sector heterogeneity, only one valuation method proved applicable. The Stage-Progression approach applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $49M total raised proxy, a standard metric for Series A-stage progression, yielding an implied valuation of $98M. A peer-median cross-check was not viable; while eight same-sector peers exist in the dataset, none satisfied the stricter filters of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparables. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given sector-specific capital intensity and development timelines.

The triangulated range, supported by the single applicable method, centers on $98M (median) with a sensitivity band of $83M to $113M. This reflects the 15% discount and premium bounds typical of single-method analysis. Key uncertainties remain material: the absence of tight-fit stage and valuation-tier peers limits the robustness of cross-validation, and Climate & Energy valuations exhibit wide dispersion based on technology maturity, capital requirements, and time-to-revenue. The $98M estimate should be stress-tested against Critical Loop's specific unit economics, pathway to Series B, and relative technology risk versus identified peers.
